paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God wants His people's whole hearts, and He says so with a love that gets hurt. Look at how He talks: He planted them like "a choice vine from the very best seed," and He asks, "Have I been a wilderness to Israel or a land of dense darkness?" (Jeremiah 2:21, 31). That's not a cold judge reading a list. I think that sounds like a heartbroken God.

Now here's the part that stings, and I'm saying it with love. His people kept saying "I have not sinned," and they cried "Rise up and save us!" only when trouble came (Jeremiah 2:35, 27). They called Him "My Father" with their mouth while they kept "doing all the evil you can" with their hands (Jeremiah 3:4-5). Friend, I've been the stamper who says "I'm fine" with smoke pouring out of the oven, and nobody fixes what they won't admit is burning.

So what do we do with this? We let God be God of the good days and the trouble days, and we stop running to things that can't pick up when we call, because He had already asked, "Where are the gods you made for yourselves?" (Jeremiah 2:28). Admitting our sin isn't the scary part, because it's the door back to the One who planted us on purpose. Check your own kitchen today, baker, and bring Him the whole batch, even the burnt ones.
